name: GQA — Grouped-Query Attention

source.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
source.authors: Ainslie, Lee-Thorp, de Jong, Zemlyanskiy, Lebrón, Sanghai (Google)

secondary.label: Llama 2 34B/70B: 'use Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) for improved inference scalability'

firstShipped.model: Falcon-40B shipped grouped KV heads (128 Q / 8 KV, 'multigroup') three days after the paper; Llama 2 70B (18 Jul 2023) is the first to name it GQA and cite the paper

problem: MQA fixes the KV bill but costs quality, and every lab in 2023 owned MHA checkpoints and a KV cache that was suddenly the serving constraint. The paper's first contribution is an uptraining recipe (MHA → MQA/GQA at ~5% of pretraining compute); its second, GQA, is a quality point between MQA and MHA.
idea: Share each K/V head across a *group* of query heads: 64 query heads → 8 KV heads is an 8× smaller cache. Convert an MHA checkpoint by mean-pooling its K/V heads into groups and 'uptraining' for ~5% of the original pretraining compute.
buys: KV cache and read traffic ÷ (heads / groups) at near-MHA quality — between MQA and MHA in quality, near MQA in speed
Retrofit-able: cheap uptraining instead of a new pretraining run
The 2023–25 default: Llama 2/3, Mistral, Qwen, gpt-oss
costs: KV is still O(context) per token — GQA lowers the constant, not the scaling
A small quality drop vs MHA on some tasks; needs the uptraining pass
Fewer KV heads constrain tensor-parallel sharding: KV heads must divide evenly or be replicated

chatbot2k.why: the baseline for any served decoder ≥7B

agent1m.why: unless you go further to MLA for an even smaller cache

pickWhen.verdict: The compromise everyone shipped. Right almost always; skip only for tiny models where KV is not the bottleneck, or when MLA is on the table.

name: RWKV — Receptance Weighted Key Value

source.title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
source.evidence: [v1] Mon, 22 May 2023 13:57:41 UTC — the RWKV-4 Pile checkpoints predate the paper (HF uploads 'RWKV-4-Pile-169M-20220807' / '430M-20220808' on 2022-08-17; repo README lists 'RWKV-4-Pile-1B5-20220903')

firstShipped.model: RWKV-4-Pile 169M/430M checkpoints on Hugging Face (the 1B5 checkpoint is dated 2022-09-03)

problem: Quadratic attention and a growing KV cache; wanted RNN-style O(1) per-token inference with transformer-style parallel training.
idea: Replace attention with a linear time-mix (WKV) plus channel-mix; trainable in parallel, run as an RNN at inference.
buys: Linear time, constant memory, no KV cache; competitive with same-size transformers up to 14B in the paper
Fully open weights and code; the community proof that the RNN was not dead
costs: Fixed state → weak exact recall / needle retrieval; prompt-order sensitivity
Kernel and serving ecosystem less mature; the paper is a post-hoc description of RWKV-4

pickWhen.verdict: Same day as GQA — the two threads of 2023 side by side: shrink the cache, or abolish it.

name: Randomized Positional Encodings

source.title: Randomized Positional Encodings Boost Length Generalization of Transformers

oneLiner: Sample positions from a range longer than the training length so the model has seen large position values — a training-time answer to extrapolation; PoSE (Sep 2023) applies the same trick to RoPE fine-tuning.
whyFootnote: Training recipe rather than an attention mechanism.

name: NoPE — no positional encoding, named and argued

source.title: The Impact of Positional Encoding on Length Generalization in Transformers
source.authors: Kazemnejad, Padhi, Ramamurthy, Das, Reddy (Mila / IBM)

secondary.label: Jamba: 'positional embeddings or mechanisms like RoPE are not necessary' (Mamba layers carry position)
Cohere Command R7B model card: 'a fourth layer uses global attention without positional embeddings'
Llama 4 iRoPE: 'interleaved attention layers without positional embeddings'

firstShipped.model: Cohere Command R7B — the first Transformer-only SWA-RoPE : NoPE-global hybrid (Jamba, Mar 2024, had already dropped positional encoding, with its Mamba layers carrying position); then Command A, Llama 4 iRoPE

problem: Which positional encoding extrapolates best — APE, T5 bias, ALiBi, RoPE, or none? Decoder-only transformers fail past training length and every PE was suspected.
idea: None. With a causal mask a decoder can recover position implicitly; NoPE can represent both absolute and relative positions in theory, and on small synthetic reasoning tasks it extrapolated at least as well as ALiBi/RoPE/T5.
buys: Nothing to break at unseen lengths; theory that NoPE can express both absolute and relative position
The licence for the NoPE-global layers of Cohere Command R7B (Dec 2024), Command A, Llama 4 iRoPE and SWAN (2025), and for DroPE
Attention learns relative-like patterns on its own
costs: Evidence is ~100M-parameter models on synthetic tasks; at LLM scale pure NoPE lags RoPE in-distribution and its length generalisation is also limited
No frequency knob: PI / NTK / YaRN cannot be applied to a NoPE layer
Decoder-only; no locality prior to exploit

chatbot2k.why: RoPE is at least as good and better understood

coding128k.why: as global layers in a hybrid

agent1m.why: as the interleaved global layers, never as the sole PE

pickWhen.verdict: Its 2023 impact was conceptual; the practical uptake came later as one half of a hybrid — Jamba dropped positional encoding in Mar 2024 with Mamba supplying position, Command R7B (Dec 2024) is the first Transformer-only NoPE-global design.

name: Position Interpolation (linear RoPE scaling)

source.title: kaiokendev, 'Things I'm Learning While Training SuperHOT' — 'Extending Context to 8K'; formalised a week later by Chen et al. (Meta), 'Extending Context Window of Large Language Models via Positional Interpolation'
source.evidence: Blog changelog: "Added 'Extending Context' (6/20/23)" — 'scaling down the frequency window in RoPE by a factor of 0.25 … these two lines are all we need to change'. Meta paper: [v1] Tue, 27 Jun 2023 16:26:26 UTC

secondary.label: Chen et al. (Meta) — Position Interpolation, arXiv 2306.15595

firstShipped.model: kaiokendev's SuperHOT-13B-8K LoRA (HF upload, RoPE scale 0.25); LongChat-16K (29 Jun) is the first lab release with the trick

problem: Everyone owned LLaMA at 2,048 tokens and RoPE explodes when extrapolated — attention scores at positions the model never saw are catastrophically large. Wanted 8–32K without a pretraining run.
idea: Do not extrapolate — interpolate. Multiply positions by 1/s so 8K positions map into the trained 0–2K range, then fine-tune briefly (kaiokendev: a 0.25 factor and a LoRA; Meta: ~1,000 steps to 32K, with a bound showing interpolation error ≈600× smaller than extrapolation).
buys: A two-line change; 7B–65B LLaMA to 32K with strong perplexity and retrieval after a short fine-tune
Short-context quality mostly preserved; became rope_scaling='linear' in every framework
Started the ten-day burst that produced NTK-aware, Dynamic NTK and, in August, YaRN
costs: Needs a fine-tune; the factor is fixed at train time
Compresses *every* frequency equally, so high-frequency (local-order) information is squeezed — a small perplexity rise at short lengths and loss of local resolution
Large factors (>8–16×) degrade — the gap NTK-by-parts / YaRN filled

rag32k.why: 2–8× with a small fine-tune; YaRN is better today

coding128k.why: the factor is too large; use YaRN or a large base

pickWhen.verdict: The community's fix arrived a week before the lab's paper. Historic now — YaRN subsumes it — but the idea 'squeeze, don't stretch' is the whole 2023 lineage.

name: PagedAttention (vLLM) — the KV cache gets virtual memory

source.title: vLLM: Easy, Fast, and Cheap LLM Serving with PagedAttention (blog); 'Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention'
source.authors: Kwon, Li, Zhuang, Sheng, Zheng, Yu, Gonzalez, Zhang, Stoica (Berkeley)
source.evidence: vLLM blog dated June 20, 2023 (vLLM v0.1); arXiv [v1] Tue, 12 Sep 2023 12:50:04 UTC

problem: Contiguous per-request KV reservation wasted 60–80% of GPU memory to fragmentation and over-reservation, capping batch size and therefore throughput. Not a math problem — a memory-management one.
idea: Store KV in fixed-size non-contiguous blocks with per-sequence block tables — an OS page table for attention — with copy-on-write for shared prefixes and parallel sampling.
buys: <4% KV waste; 2–4× throughput vs FasterTransformer/Orca; up to 24× vs HF Transformers
Prefix sharing became the basis of 'prompt caching'
costs: Pure serving change: attention semantics, compute and context length untouched
Block indirection in kernels; later work (vAttention) argues the paging indirection itself has overhead versus contiguous virtual memory

pickWhen.verdict: Not a modelling decision — but it is the moment 'KV memory' became the number everyone optimises against, and every 2024 mechanism is measured in its units.

name: H2O — heavy-hitter KV eviction

source.title: H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models

problem: The KV cache grows linearly during decode; a few 'heavy-hitter' tokens carry most cumulative attention.
idea: Keep the heavy hitters plus a recent window and evict the rest — no training.
buys: 5–10× smaller KV at small accuracy loss; large throughput gains at the time
costs: Lossy and irreversible; cumulative-score bias toward early tokens
Needs materialised attention scores — fights FlashAttention-style kernels
Degrades on exact long-range retrieval; superseded by SnapKV / quantisation

rag32k.why: memory-bound generation that tolerates approximate recall

pickWhen.verdict: The 'evict' branch of the KV bill (vs share = GQA/CLA, compress = MLA, quantise = KIVI). Same week as vLLM.

name: NTK-aware scaled RoPE
aka: NTK scaling; 'change the RoPE base' θ' = θ·α^{d/(d−2)}

source.title: NTK-Aware Scaled RoPE allows LLaMA models to have extended (8k+) context size without any fine-tuning and minimal perplexity degradation (r/LocalLLaMA)
source.evidence: Reddit post 14lz7j5, created_utc 1688026889 = 2023-06-29 08:21 UTC (archive record); HF TGI issue #512 with the same title opened 30 Jun 2023; cited by the YaRN paper and the EleutherAI 'Extending the RoPE' blog. Not a paper — a Reddit post.

problem: PI without a fine-tune wrecked perplexity: it compresses every RoPE frequency equally and destroys the high-frequency dimensions that encode local order. Wanted a zero-fine-tune stretch.
idea: Do not scale positions; scale the *base*. Raising θ interpolates the low-frequency dimensions (which see the new far distances) while the high-frequency dimensions barely change — the NTK / Fourier-features intuition that high frequencies are what a network needs to resolve nearby tokens. A three-line change.
buys: LLaMA-7B to 8K+ with minor perplexity loss and no fine-tuning
The intuition that trained-in base scaling (Code Llama 1e6, Llama 3 500K) then made standard
Direct lineage: NTK-aware → Dynamic NTK → NTK-by-parts → YaRN
costs: A static α must be picked for a target length and slightly hurts short-context perplexity
Some dimensions still extrapolate past their trained range, so it fine-tunes worse than 'by-parts'
It is a Reddit post with perplexity plots — the citable versions are YaRN and the EleutherAI blog; 'NTK' is a loose name

rag32k.why: quick zero-fine-tune 2–4× stretch of an existing model

coding128k.why: bake a large base in if you can train; else YaRN

pickWhen.verdict: The most influential Reddit post in the field: it found the right knob (θ) in a weekend, and the labs shipped it trained-in within two months.

name: Dynamic NTK (dynamically scaled RoPE)

source.title: Dynamically Scaled RoPE further increases performance of long context LLaMA with zero fine-tuning (r/LocalLLaMA)
source.evidence: Reddit post 14mrgpr, created_utc 1688103246 = 2023-06-30 05:34 UTC (evening of 29 June in US time zones), ~21 hours after bloc97's post; cited by the YaRN paper (§3.3 'Dynamic Scaling')

problem: A static factor degrades short sequences and targets one length. Wanted one deployed model that behaves normally at ≤2K and degrades gracefully as the input grows.
idea: Compute the scale from the *current* sequence length: α = 1 below the trained length, then grows with L′/L. No change for short inputs, progressively scaled RoPE for long ones.
buys: Better perplexity-vs-length curve than static NTK or PI; zero training; trivial at inference
costs: Changing the base mid-generation makes already-cached keys inconsistent with new ones — recompute or accept the mismatch
Still falls apart beyond a few-× extension; an inference hack that gives no training signal

rag32k.why: a 4K model seeing 6–8K without crashing quality; not a way to reach 32K

pickWhen.verdict: The overflow valve. Right for serving a fixed-context model that occasionally sees more; not a way to build long context.

name: LongNet — dilated attention

source.title: LongNet: Scaling Transformers to 1,000,000,000 Tokens

oneLiner: Exponentially dilated sparse pattern with a '1B tokens' headline; little adoption.
whyFootnote: Fixed-pattern sparsity, already represented by Sparse Transformer / Longformer.

name: RetNet — retention with exponential decay

source.title: Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models
source.authors: Sun, Dong, Huang, Ma, Xia, Xue, Wang, Wei (Microsoft)
source.evidence: [v1] Mon, 17 Jul 2023 16:40:01 UTC — same day as FlashAttention-2

problem: The 'impossible triangle': training parallelism, O(1) per-token inference, transformer quality.
idea: Retention = linear attention with a per-head exponential decay (xPos-style); the same weights run parallel (training), recurrent (decode) or chunkwise (long sequences).
buys: ~8× decode throughput and much lower memory vs a KV-cache transformer at 7B/8K; competitive perplexity to 6.7B
The parallel/recurrent/chunkwise triality every later linear layer uses
costs: Fixed, input-independent decay → limited long-range recall
No data-dependent gating (GLA / Mamba added it); no mainstream adoption; 'successor to Transformer' did not pan out

agent1m.why: as a research baseline; pick GLA / Mamba-2 / GDN hybrids instead

pickWhen.verdict: The linear thread's 2023 opening bid; overtaken within six months by gated versions.

name: Softmax-1 — 'Attention Is Off By One'
aka: quiet attention; ghost attention; +1 in the denominator

source.title: Attention Is Off By One
source.evidence: Blog page dated July 24, 2023 — two months before StreamingLLM; gpt-oss's model card cites it alongside Xiao et al.

firstShipped.model: gpt-oss (learned per-head bias in the softmax denominator, 'similar to off-by-one attention and attention sinks')

problem: Softmax forces every head to put its weight somewhere, so heads with nothing to say park it on no-op tokens — delimiters and whitespace in Miller's telling, following Bondarenko et al.; later shown to be mostly the first token — producing massive-activation outliers that wreck low-bit quantisation.
idea: softmax₁(x)_i = exp(x_i) / (1 + Σ_j exp(x_j)): give the head a way to abstain. The 'sink' becomes an explicit escape hatch instead of the BOS token.
buys: Heads can output ≈0; fewer outliers; cheaper quantisation; a principled place to put the sink
costs: A blog with no large-scale experiments; the constant 1 is arbitrary (gpt-oss made it a learned per-head logit)
Cannot be retrofitted; StreamingLLM found sinks form anyway and can simply be kept

chatbot2k.why: new pretraining runs that want quantisation- and window-friendly attention

pickWhen.verdict: A blog restatement — after Bondarenko et al. (Jun 2023) — of the 'let a head abstain' fix, two months before StreamingLLM named the sink. It reached production, renamed, in gpt-oss.

secondary.label: Bondarenko et al., 'Quantizable Transformers: Removing Outliers by Helping Attention Heads Do Nothing' (clipped softmax / gated attention)

name: ReRoPE / LM-Infinite / SelfExtend — training-free RoPE remapping

source.title: ReRoPE (Su Jianlin, bojone/rerope); LM-Infinite (Han et al., 2308.16137); SelfExtend (Jin et al., 2401.01325)
source.authors: Su Jianlin; Han et al.; Jin et al.
source.evidence: ReRoPE repo first commit 2023-08-07T01:54:42Z ('Create ntk_patch.py'); LM-Infinite [v1] Wed, 30 Aug 2023 16:47:51 UTC; SelfExtend [v1] Tue, 2 Jan 2024; llama.cpp merged Self-Extend 2024-01-08 (PR #4815)

secondary.label: SelfExtend (grouped far positions + exact neighbour positions)

problem: Attention explodes at unseen relative distances and models 'forget' the start; wanted extrapolation with zero training on a pretrained RoPE model.
idea: ReRoPE (Aug 2023) clamps relative positions beyond a window; LM-Infinite (Aug 2023) uses a Λ-shaped mask — the first tokens plus a recent window — with a distance ceiling; SelfExtend (Jan 2024) floor-divides far positions into groups while keeping exact neighbour positions. Three variants of one rule: never present a distance the model was not trained on.
buys: Flat perplexity to very long inputs; SelfExtend keeps passkey retrieval intact at ~3× (Mistral 8K → 24K) and is usable at 4–6× on long-context benchmarks; shipped in llama.cpp
costs: Far tokens get blurred, coarse positions; ReRoPE and SelfExtend need two attention passes (~2× prefill) unless fused; LM-Infinite is a single cheaper pass (2.7× faster decode at 32K) but drops mid-context tokens unless its optional top-k middle attention is on
All obsolete once you can train long context

rag32k.why: hobbyist inference of a short-context checkpoint

pickWhen.verdict: How RoPE fails, taught by fixing it for free; not frontier production.

name: RoPE base-frequency scaling, trained in (Code Llama θ=1e6; later named 'ABF' by Xiong et al.)

source.title: Code Llama: Open Foundation Models for Code — 'we increase the base period θ from 10,000 to 1,000,000 for fine-tuning'
source.evidence: [v1] Thu, 24 Aug 2023 17:39:13 UTC (model released the same day); the name 'ABF' comes from Llama 2 Long (2309.16039, [v1] Wed, 27 Sep 2023)

secondary.label: Llama 3: 'We increase the RoPE base frequency hyperparameter to 500,000'

problem: Repository-level code needs long inputs; PI squeezes positions and hurts local resolution. If you are fine-tuning anyway, is there a cleaner lever?
idea: The trained-in cousin of NTK-aware: raise θ (10K → 1M) and fine-tune on 16K sequences. Low-frequency dims now rotate slowly enough to cover the new length; short-context quality is mostly kept (a small measured drop).
buys: One config line; extrapolates beyond training length better than linear PI ('improvements on inputs with up to 100k tokens')
Became the default recipe: Llama 3 (500K), Qwen (1M+) — the number you see in every config.json
costs: Needs a long-sequence fine-tune stage; the price is a small short-context regression (−0.5 pt HumanEval, −1.9 pt MBPP, up to −2 BLEU on <4K prompts) — perplexity keeps falling well past the 16K training length and only creeps up beyond ~100K
θ is chosen heuristically; low-frequency dims are undertrained (later refined per-dim by YaRN / LongRoPE)

chatbot2k.why: set a large base from the start

pickWhen.verdict: If you will train on long data anyway, this is what everyone does. Use NTK/YaRN/DCA only when you cannot.

name: YaRN — Yet another RoPE extensioN

source.title: YaRN: Efficient Context Window Extension of Large Language Models

secondary.label: DeepSeek-V2: 'we employ YaRN to extend the default context window length from 4K to 128K' (s=40, α=1, β=32)

firstShipped.model: Yarn-Llama-2-7b/13b-64k/128k from the authors at release; DeepSeek-V2 (May 2024) is the first frontier-lab base model to ship with YaRN

problem: PI needs many fine-tune tokens and hurts short context; NTK-aware still extrapolates some dimensions. Wanted a principled per-frequency scheme, and a fix for the softmax entropy shift that appears at long lengths.
idea: NTK-by-parts: leave high-frequency dims untouched, interpolate low-frequency dims, ramp in between; plus scale attention logits by a temperature (folded into RoPE) to keep the softmax's entropy where it was trained. Works in a dynamic, no-fine-tune mode too.
buys: ~10× fewer tokens and ~2.5× fewer steps than PI; Llama 2 to 128K
Consolidates the whole Reddit lineage into one citable paper; rope_scaling='yarn' in every framework
What DeepSeek-V2 and Qwen2.5 actually use for >32K
costs: Still a fine-tune (small); extra hyperparameters (α, β, s, temperature)
Short-context perplexity still rises slightly; quality beyond the target length degrades
Needs framework support; a patch on RoPE, not a new position scheme

rag32k.why: 4–32× extension of an existing model with a modest budget

agent1m.why: works, but 1M-class models mostly train long or interleave NoPE

pickWhen.verdict: The best way to stretch a RoPE model you already have. If you are pretraining, just use a big base and a long-context stage.

name: PoSE — Positional Skip-wise training

source.title: PoSE: Efficient Context Window Extension of LLMs via Positional Skip-wise Training

oneLiner: Simulate long positions in short training windows by skipping position ids — extend context without long training sequences.
whyFootnote: Training recipe on top of RoPE scaling.

name: Sliding window attention in a mainstream LLM — Mistral 7B

source.title: Mistral 7B (announcement); paper 'Mistral 7B'
source.evidence: Mistral blog dated September 27, 2023: 'each layer attends to the previous 4,096 hidden states', KV cache 'limited to a size of sliding_window tokens, using rotating buffers'; paper [v1] Tue, 10 Oct 2023 17:54:58 UTC

problem: Serve a 7B model with a bounded KV cache and handle inputs longer than 4K on modest hardware.
idea: Every layer attends to the previous W=4,096 tokens only; the KV cache is a rolling buffer of W entries. Information still propagates ~W × layers through depth. Combined with GQA.
buys: Attention cost and KV cache bounded by W regardless of input length (rolling buffer halves the cache at 8K)
Longformer's idea finally in a mainstream decoder, with weights anyone could run
Brought GQA to the popular 7B size (Falcon-40B, Code Llama 34B and Falcon-180B had shipped it before)
costs: Beyond the window, information flows only indirectly through stacked layers → poor exact recall far back
Window fixed at train time
Mistral itself moved later versions to full attention — evidence it hurt long-range tasks; the pattern survived only as the *local* half of interleaved designs

chatbot2k.why: cheap serving where local context dominates

pickWhen.verdict: Right as one half of a local:global stack (Gemma 2/3, gpt-oss); wrong as the whole story — and Mistral's own retreat says so.

name: Attention sinks — StreamingLLM
aka: sink tokens; sink + sliding-window KV; learned attention sink

source.title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
source.authors: Xiao, Tian, Chen, Han, Lewis (MIT / Meta / CMU)

secondary.label: Massive Activations in LLMs — the mechanism behind sinks
gpt-oss: learned per-head sink bias in the softmax denominator

firstShipped.model: gpt-oss-120b/20b (learned sink) — engineering uptake in HF/TensorRT-LLM from Oct 2023

problem: Streaming decode with a finite KV cache: the moment plain sliding-window eviction drops the first tokens, perplexity collapses; recomputation is too slow.
idea: The first ~4 tokens are where softmax dumps its excess attention (the 'sink'). Keep them forever plus a rolling window, re-index positions inside the cache, and generation stays stable — the paper also proposes a dedicated trainable sink token.
buys: Stable perplexity over 4M tokens on Llama-2 / MPT / Falcon / Pythia; ~22× faster than sliding-window-with-recompute
Explains the phenomenon (Massive Activations, Feb 2024, gives the mechanism) and turns it into a design rule
gpt-oss (Aug 2025) bakes the sink in as a learned per-head logit
costs: No real long-range memory: evicted content is gone — it is not a context-length extension for retrieval
Positions must be re-indexed inside the cache
The benefit is stability and latency, not capability

rag32k.why: not for QA over the whole document

agent1m.why: as the eviction rule inside a bounded-cache layer; never as the memory

pickWhen.verdict: It buys infinite *streaming*, not infinite *context*. Right for a chat that never ends; wrong for an agent that must remember page one.

name: Ring Attention — exact attention sharded across devices

source.title: Ring Attention with Blockwise Transformers for Near-Infinite Context

firstShipped.model: Large World Model (1M-token text/video, same authors)

problem: Per-device memory caps sequence length even with FlashAttention; wanted *exact* attention over sequences that scale with device count.
idea: Split the sequence across devices; each computes blockwise attention on its query block while K/V blocks rotate around a ring, overlapping communication with compute.
buys: Exact attention over millions of tokens; memory per device independent of total length
The 'context parallelism' used to train 128K–1M models
costs: Does not reduce total FLOPs (still quadratic) — only distributes them
Needs many devices and fast interconnect; causal load imbalance (fixed by Striped Attention)

agent1m.why: training or serving 1M+ on multi-GPU — necessary, still pays n²

pickWhen.verdict: The systems answer to length: pay the whole bill, but split it across the room.

name: FIRE — functional interpolation for relative positions

source.title: Functional Interpolation for Relative Positions Improves Long Context Transformers
source.authors: Li, You, Guruganesh, Ainslie, Ontanon, Zaheer, Sanghai, Yang, Kumar, Bhojanapalli (Google)

problem: Learn the bias shape instead of hand-picking it (ALiBi, KERPLE), and keep its input in-range at any length.
idea: An MLP of relative distance normalised by the query position (progressive interpolation), so the input stays in [0,1]; unifies T5 bias, ALiBi and KERPLE as special cases.
buys: Strong zero-shot length generalisation on perplexity and long-context tasks
costs: Per-pair MLP adds compute; additive bias vs fused kernels
No frontier adoption — RoPE ecosystem inertia

pickWhen.verdict: Endpoint of the learned-bias branch that lost to 'RoPE + scaling'.

name: Mamba — selective state space model

source.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces

firstShipped.model: AI21 Jamba — 'first production-grade Mamba based model', SSM-Transformer hybrid, 256K

problem: Transformers are quadratic with a growing KV cache; prior SSMs (S4/H3) were linear but could not select by content and lagged on language.
idea: Make the SSM parameters (Δ, B, C) input-dependent so the state can selectively remember or forget, and run it with a hardware-aware parallel scan.
buys: ~5× decode throughput, constant state, linear in length; matched transformers ~2× its size at ≤2.8B
One homogeneous block; the SSM thread's breakout paper
costs: Weak in-context copying / exact retrieval — no KV cache to look things up in
Custom kernels; the scan is not tensor-core friendly (Mamba-2 fixes this)
In practice needs a few attention layers (hybrids) to be competitive

pickWhen.verdict: The recurrent thread's loudest 2023 paper. Mamba-2 later showed that a restricted selective SSM (scalar decay) is exactly a form of gated linear attention — a refinement, not an identity.

name: Gated Linear Attention (GLA) + FlashLinearAttention

source.title: Gated Linear Attention Transformers with Hardware-Efficient Training
source.authors: Yang, Wang, Shen, Panda, Kim (MIT / IBM)

firstShipped.model: Not directly; its descendant Gated DeltaNet (same lead author) ships in Qwen3-Next

problem: Linear attention underperformed softmax and had no hardware-efficient training path; Mamba showed data-dependent gating matters but its scan is not tensor-core friendly.
idea: Linear attention with data-dependent (matrix-valued) forget gates, trained with a chunkwise algorithm that trades memory movement for tensor-core matmuls (FlashLinearAttention).
buys: At 340M–1.3B matches LLaMA-architecture and Mamba on LM benchmarks with better length generalisation and constant-memory decode
The chunkwise-parallel recipe (and the fla library) that every later linear layer — DeltaNet, GDN, KDA — is trained with
costs: Fixed-size state → weak on recall-intensive tasks vs softmax; paper scale ≤1.3B
GLA itself never shipped; only descendant layers (Gated DeltaNet, KDA) did, always inside hybrids with some full-attention layers; custom Triton kernels

agent1m.why: as the linear layers of a hybrid

pickWhen.verdict: The bridge from RetNet to Gated DeltaNet — gating plus a training algorithm the hardware likes.

name: RadixAttention / prefix caching (SGLang)

source.title: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs

oneLiner: Cross-request KV reuse via a radix tree — the systems idea behind API 'prompt caching'. Pairs with PagedAttention.
whyFootnote: Serving systems, not an attention mechanism.
